metadata.title: A constructive proof of the general Lovasz Local Lemma

nodes.name: Lovasz Local Lemma (general form)
nodes.statement: If $\exists x: \mathcal{A} \to (0,1)$ with $\pr[A] \le x(A) \prod_{B \in \Gamma(A)}(1-x(B))$ for all $A \in \mathcal{A}$, then $\pr[\bigcap_A \bar A] \ge \prod_A (1-x(A)) > 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Classical Lovasz Local Lemma: a finite family of events with bounded dependencies and small probabilities can be simultaneously avoided with positive probability.
assumptions: $\mathcal{A}$ is a finite set of events

nodes.name: Determining variable set vbl(A)
nodes.statement: For an event $A$ determined by $\mathcal{P}$, $\mbox{vbl}(A)$ denotes the unique minimal $S \subseteq \mathcal{P}$ that determines $A$.

nodes.name: Dependency graph $G_{\mathcal{A}}$
nodes.statement: Graph on vertex set $\mathcal{A}$ with an edge between $A \ne B$ iff $\mbox{vbl}(A) \cap \mbox{vbl}(B) \ne \emptyset$. $\Gamma(A)$ is the neighborhood of $A$ in $G$.

nodes.name: Violation and resampling
nodes.statement: An evaluation of $\mbox{vbl}(A)$ \emph{violates} $A$ if it makes $A$ happen. A \emph{resampling} of $A$ takes a fresh independent sample of every variable in $\mbox{vbl}(A)$.

nodes.name: Inclusive neighborhood $\Gamma^+(A)$
nodes.statement: $\Gamma^+(A) := \Gamma(A) \cup \{A\}$.

nodes.name: Execution log $C$
nodes.statement: $C : \mathbb{N} \to \mathcal{A}$ lists the events selected for resampling at each step of the algorithm; if the algorithm terminates, $C$ is partial.

nodes.name: Witness tree $\tau = (T, \sigma_T)$
nodes.statement: A finite rooted tree $T$ with labelling $\sigma_T : V(T) \to \mathcal{A}$ such that the children of any vertex $u$ receive labels from $\Gamma^+(\sigma_T(u))$. Proper if distinct siblings carry distinct labels.

nodes.name: Witness tree $\tau_C(t)$ associated with step $t$
nodes.statement: Built backwards from log $C$: start with isolated root labelled $C(t)$; for $i = t-1,\ldots,1$, if some vertex $v \in \tau_C^{(i+1)}(t)$ has $C(i) \in \Gamma^+([v])$, attach a child labelled $C(i)$ to the deepest such $v$. Set $\tau_C(t) := \tau_C^{(1)}(t)$.

nodes.name: Occurrence of a witness tree in a log
nodes.statement: $\tau$ \emph{occurs} in $C$ if $\tau_C(t) = \tau$ for some $t \in \mathbb{N}$.

nodes.name: Galton-Watson process for proper witness trees
nodes.statement: Multitype branching process: round 1 produces a singleton root labelled $A$; in each later round, each existing vertex $v$ independently spawns, for every $B \in \Gamma^+([v])$, a child labelled $B$ with probability $x(B)$ and skips it with probability $1-x(B)$.

nodes.name: Modified weight $x'(B)$
nodes.statement: $x'(B) := x(B) \prod_{C \in \Gamma(B)}(1-x(C))$.

nodes.name: Depth of a witness tree
nodes.statement: The maximal depth of a vertex in a witness tree $\tau$ (distance from the root).

nodes.name: Consistency of a witness tree with deterministic samples
nodes.statement: A witness tree $\tau$ is \emph{consistent} with sequences $(v_i^{(j)})$ if the $\tau$-check passes when these sequences replace the random source.

nodes.name: Lopsidependence and lopsidependency graph
nodes.statement: $A,B$ are \emph{lopsidependent} if $\exists$ evaluations $f,g$ differing only on $\mbox{vbl}(A) \cap \mbox{vbl}(B)$ with $f$ violating $A$, $g$ violating $B$, but $f$ does not violate $B$ or $g$ does not violate $A$. The lopsidependency graph has $\mathcal{A}$ as vertices, neighborhoods $\Gamma'(A)$.

nodes.name: Elementary event
nodes.statement: $A \in \mathcal{A}$ is \emph{elementary} if a single evaluation of $\mbox{vbl}(A)$ violates $A$. For elementary events, lopsidependence reduces to mutual exclusion.

nodes.name: Lopsided witness tree $\varrho_C(t)$
nodes.statement: Built like $\tau_C(t)$ but the children of a vertex labelled $A$ are drawn from $\Gamma'^+(A) := \Gamma'(A) \cup \{A\}$ instead of $\Gamma^+(A)$.

nodes.name: Sequential LLL solver (Algorithm 1.1)
nodes.statement: Sample all variables uniformly; while some event $A \in \mathcal{A}$ is violated, pick one and resample $\mbox{vbl}(A)$; return the final assignment.
input: Finite set $\mathcal{P}$ of mutually independent random variables
Finite family $\mathcal{A}$ of events determined by $\mathcal{P}$, each with $\mbox{vbl}(A)$
output: Evaluation $(v_P)_{P \in \mathcal{P}}$ that violates no event in $\mathcal{A}$

nodes.name: Parallel LLL solver (Algorithm 1.2)
nodes.statement: Same as Algorithm 1.1 but in each round resample, in parallel, the variables of a maximal independent set $S$ of currently violated events in $G_{\mathcal{A}}$.
input: Finite set $\mathcal{P}$ of mutually independent random variables
An MIS subroutine for the violated subgraph (e.g. Luby's algorithm)

nodes.name: Deterministic LLL solver via conditional expectations
nodes.statement: Enumerate witness trees of size in $[c \log m, (k+1) c \log m]$; greedily fix sample values $v_i^{(j)}$ to keep the expected number of consistent trees $\le 1/2$; then run Algorithm 1.1/1.2 on the fixed samples.
input: Family $\mathcal{A}$ of $m$ events with bounded-degree dependency graph ($|\Gamma(A)| \le k$)
Oracle for conditional probabilities $\pr[A \mid \forall i \in I: P_i = v_i]$ in time poly$(s)$
Constants $\varepsilon > 0$, $x : \mathcal{A} \to (0,1)$ satisfying the strengthened LLL condition
output: Deterministic evaluation $(v_i)$ of $\mathcal{P}$ such that no event in $\mathcal{A}$ occurs
Total runtime polynomial in $s = m + n + \sum_i |D_i|$

nodes.name: $\tau$-check
nodes.statement: Visit vertices of $\tau$ in order of non-increasing depth; for each $v$ draw a fresh independent sample of $\mbox{vbl}([v])$ and test whether $[v]$ is violated. Pass iff every event was violated when checked.
input: Independent random samples for each variable
output: Boolean: pass (all events violated when checked) or fail

nodes.name: Luby's MIS algorithm
nodes.statement: Randomized parallel algorithm computing a maximal independent set in any graph in expected $O(\log n)$ time, with one processor per vertex.

nodes.name: Main theorem (sequential algorithm correctness)
nodes.statement: Under the LLL condition $\pr[A] \le x(A) \prod_{B \in \Gamma(A)}(1-x(B))$, Algorithm 1.1 finds an evaluation violating no event, and the expected number of resamplings of $A$ is at most $x(A)/(1-x(A))$, totalling at most $\sum_A x(A)/(1-x(A))$.
assumptions: $\mathcal{P}$ finite set of mutually independent random variables
$\mathcal{A}$ finite set of events determined by $\mathcal{P}$
conclusions: There exists an evaluation of $\mathcal{P}$ violating no event in $\mathcal{A}$
Algorithm 1.1 resamples each $A$ at most $x(A)/(1-x(A))$ times in expectation

nodes.name: Parallel algorithm runtime bound
nodes.statement: If $\pr[A] \le (1-\varepsilon) x(A) \prod_{B \in \Gamma(A)}(1-x(B))$ for some $\varepsilon > 0$, the parallel algorithm terminates in expected $O(\frac{1}{\varepsilon} \log \sum_A \frac{x(A)}{1-x(A)})$ steps.
conclusions: Parallel algorithm finds a non-violating evaluation in expected $O(\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\log\sum_A \frac{x(A)}{1-x(A)})$ steps

nodes.name: Deterministic LLL theorem
nodes.statement: If $|\Gamma(A)| \le k$ for all $A$ (constant $k$), conditional probabilities are computable in poly$(s)$ time, and $(1-\varepsilon) x(A) \prod_B(1-x(B))$ bounds $\pr[A]$ for some constant $\varepsilon > 0$, then a deterministic algorithm finds a non-violating evaluation in poly$(s)$ time.
assumptions: Conditional probabilities $\pr[A \mid \forall i \in I: P_i = v_i]$ computable in poly$(s)$
conclusions: A deterministic algorithm finds an evaluation of $\mathcal{P}$ violating no event, in time poly$(s)$

nodes.name: Lopsided LLL (lopsidependency version of main theorem)
nodes.statement: If $\pr[A] \le x(A) \prod_{B \in \Gamma'(A)}(1-x(B))$ where $\Gamma'$ is the lopsidependency neighborhood, then Algorithm 1.1 still finds a non-violating evaluation with the same expected resampling bounds.
conclusions: Algorithm 1.1 resamples each $A$ at most $x(A)/(1-x(A))$ times in expectation

nodes.name: Coupling lemma for witness trees
nodes.statement: (i) If $\tau$ occurs in $C$ then $\tau$ is proper. (ii) The probability that $\tau$ appears in $C$ is at most $\prod_{v \in V(\tau)} \pr[[v]]$.
assumptions: $C$ the random log produced by Algorithm 1.1
conclusions: If $\tau$ occurs in $C$, then $\tau$ is proper

nodes.name: Galton-Watson tree probability formula
nodes.statement: For a fixed proper witness tree $\tau$ with root labelled $A$, the probability that the Galton-Watson process produces exactly $\tau$ is $p_\tau = \frac{1-x(A)}{x(A)} \prod_{v \in V(\tau)} x'([v])$.
assumptions: $\tau$ a fixed proper witness tree with root labelled $A$
Galton-Watson process as in Definition DP289.9

nodes.name: Parallel-step depth lemma
nodes.statement: If $t \in S_j$ (segment of the sequentialised log corresponding to parallel step $j$), then $\tau_C(t)$ has depth $j-1$.
assumptions: Segments $S_j$ of the sequentialised log of an execution of the parallel algorithm

nodes.name: Small-witness shrinkage lemma
nodes.statement: If the dependency graph has max degree $\le k$ and some witness tree of size $\ge u$ is consistent with the sequences, then a consistent witness tree of size in $[u, (k+1)u]$ also exists.
assumptions: Maximum degree of dependency graph bounded by $k$
There exists a witness tree of size $\ge u$ consistent with $(v_i^{(j)})$
conclusions: There exists a consistent witness tree of size in $[u, (k+1)u]$

nodes.name: Lopsided coupling lemma
nodes.statement: For a fixed proper lopsided witness tree $\tau$ and the random log $C$, $\pr[\exists t: \tau = \varrho_C(t)] \le \prod_{v \in V(\tau)} \pr[[v]]$.

nodes.name: Proof of coupling lemma
nodes.statement: Coupling argument: assume $\tau = \tau_C(t)$. Show labels at equal depth are independent (proves properness); then show that running the $\tau$-check on the algorithm's random source always passes, yielding the probability bound.

nodes.name: Depth monotonicity from independence
nodes.statement: If $q(u)<q(v)$ and $\mbox{vbl}([u]) \cap \mbox{vbl}([v]) \ne \emptyset$ then $d(u) > d(v)$, since $u$ is attached to $v$ or to a vertex of equal/greater depth.

nodes.name: Properness of $\tau$ (claim (i))
nodes.statement: Vertices at equal depth in $\tau$ have labels with disjoint variable sets, hence form an independent set in $G$; in particular $\tau$ is proper.

nodes.name: Define the $\tau$-check procedure
nodes.statement: Visit vertices of $\tau$ in non-increasing depth order; at each $v$ draw fresh samples of $\mbox{vbl}([v])$ and test violation. Pass probability is exactly $\prod_{v} \pr[[v]]$.

nodes.name: Couple algorithm with $\tau$-check via shared random sequences
nodes.statement: Use a shared infinite list of independent samples $P^{(0)}, P^{(1)}, \ldots$ for each variable; both procedures consume samples in order.

nodes.name: Sample-index match at vertex $v$
nodes.statement: When the $\tau$-check considers $v$, it consumes $P^{(|S(P)|)}$ for each $P \in \mbox{vbl}([v])$; this matches the algorithm's value at step $q(v)$.

nodes.name: Conclude $\tau$-check passes whenever $\tau$ occurs
nodes.statement: Since the algorithm finds $[v]$ violated at step $q(v)$ and the $\tau$-check uses the same values, $[v]$ is violated in the check too; hence $\pr[\tau \text{ occurs}] \le \pr[\tau\text{-check passes}] = \prod_{v} \pr[[v]]$.

nodes.name: Proof of main theorem
nodes.statement: Bound $\mathbb{E}(N_A)$ by summing the witness-tree probabilities from the coupling lemma; rewrite the sum using the Galton-Watson formula to obtain $\mathbb{E}(N_A) \le x(A)/(1-x(A))$.

nodes.name: Identify $N_A$ with number of distinct proper witness trees rooted at $A$
nodes.statement: Each occurrence of $A$ in the log $C$ produces a distinct proper witness tree rooted at $A$ (the $i$-th occurrence yields a tree with $i$ vertices labelled $A$).

nodes.name: Bound $\mathbb{E}(N_A)$ using coupling lemma
nodes.statement: $\mathbb{E}(N_A) = \sum_{\tau \in \mathcal{T}_A} \pr[\tau\text{ in }C] \le \sum_{\tau} \prod_v \pr[[v]] \le \sum_\tau \prod_v x'([v])$, by Lemma LP289.1 and the LLL hypothesis.

nodes.name: Rewrite via Galton-Watson probabilities
nodes.statement: By Lemma LP289.2, $\sum_\tau \prod_v x'([v]) = \frac{x(A)}{1-x(A)} \sum_\tau p_\tau \le \frac{x(A)}{1-x(A)}$ since $\sum_\tau p_\tau \le 1$.

nodes.name: Conclude finite-expected-time termination
nodes.statement: $\mathbb{E}[\text{total resamplings}] \le \sum_A x(A)/(1-x(A)) < \infty$, so Algorithm 1.1 terminates almost surely with a non-violating evaluation.

nodes.name: Proof of GW probability lemma
nodes.statement: Direct calculation: write $p_\tau$ as $\frac{1}{x(A)}\prod_v(x([v])\prod_{u \in W_v}(1-x([u])))$; rewrite using inclusive then exclusive neighborhoods to obtain $\frac{1-x(A)}{x(A)}\prod_v x'([v])$.

nodes.name: Proof of parallel theorem
nodes.statement: Use Lemma LP289.3: if the parallel algorithm runs $\ge k$ steps, some witness tree of depth $k-1$ (and hence $\ge k$ vertices) occurs; sum over $\mathcal{T}_A(k)$ to get $Q(k) \le (1-\varepsilon)^k \sum_A x(A)/(1-x(A))$, which yields the $O(\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\log(\cdot))$ expected runtime.

nodes.name: Sequentialise the parallel execution
nodes.statement: Order the events resampled in each parallel step arbitrarily; segments $S_j$ of the resulting sequential log correspond to parallel step $j$.

nodes.name: Apply depth lemma
nodes.statement: By Lemma LP289.3, if the parallel algorithm runs $\ge k$ steps then some witness tree of depth $k-1$, hence with $\ge k$ vertices, occurs in the log.

nodes.name: Bound $Q(k)$ by tail of weighted tree sum
nodes.statement: $Q(k) \le \sum_A \sum_{\tau \in \mathcal{T}_A(k)} \prod_v \pr[[v]] \le (1-\varepsilon)^k \sum_A \sum_{\tau \in \mathcal{T}_A} \prod_v x'([v])$ using the strengthened LLL hypothesis $|V(\tau)| \ge k$.

nodes.name: Convert to closed form via Galton-Watson formula
nodes.statement: Using Lemma LP289.2 again, $Q(k) \le (1-\varepsilon)^k \sum_A \frac{x(A)}{1-x(A)}$. Summing $\sum_k Q(k)$ yields the $O(\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\log \sum_A \frac{x(A)}{1-x(A)})$ expected step count.

nodes.name: Proof of parallel-step depth lemma
nodes.statement: By backward induction on $k$: $\tau_j$ is a single-vertex root (independence); each step from $\tau_{k+1}$ to $\tau_k$ adds vertices of independent labels and increments the depth by exactly one (otherwise some violated event was missed by the chosen MIS).

nodes.name: Proof of deterministic theorem
nodes.statement: Bound the expected number of large consistent witness trees; use Lemma LP289.4 to keep the relevant tree list polynomial; greedily fix samples by conditional expectations to drive the count to zero; then run Algorithm 1.1/1.2.

nodes.name: Bound weights away from 1
nodes.statement: Replace $x(A)$ by $\tilde x(A) := (1-\varepsilon/2)x(A)$ and $\varepsilon$ by $\varepsilon/2$; the LLL hypothesis still holds and the new weights are bounded above by $1-\varepsilon/2$.

nodes.name: Choose threshold $c \log m$
nodes.statement: Expected number of consistent witness trees of size $\ge k$ is $O(m(1-\varepsilon)^k)$; choose constant $c$ so that for $k \ge c \log m$ this expectation is $\le 1/2$.

nodes.name: Restrict attention to trees in $[c\log m, (k+1)c\log m]$
nodes.statement: By Lemma LP289.4, it suffices to forbid consistent witness trees of size in $[c \log m, (k+1) c \log m]$; under bounded degree this list $L$ has polynomial length.

nodes.name: Conditional expectations to fix samples
nodes.statement: Iterate over $(i,j)$ with $1 \le i \le n$, $0 \le j \le c \log m$; at each step pick $v_i^{(j)} \in D_i$ minimising the conditional expected number of consistent trees in $L$, preserving the upper bound $1/2$.

nodes.name: Compute tree probabilities efficiently
nodes.statement: For each $\tau \in L$, traverse bottom-up; at each vertex multiply the conditional probability of the corresponding event being violated (using the assumed oracle) to obtain the consistency probability.

nodes.name: Conclude polynomial-time termination
nodes.statement: After preprocessing, no consistent tree of size $\ge c \log m$ exists, so the randomized algorithm with these fixed samples terminates after $O(\log m)$ resamplings per variable, hence poly$(s)$ total time.

nodes.name: Proof of small-witness shrinkage lemma
nodes.statement: Smallest counterexample $\tau$ of size $> (k+1)u$. Visit children $w_1,\ldots,w_j$ ($j \le k+1$) of root; take a bottom-up log $C'$ of length $|\tau|$; some sub-witness $\tau_i$ has $\ge (|\tau|-1)/(k+1) \ge u$ vertices, contradicting minimality.

nodes.name: Proof of lopsided coupling lemma
nodes.statement: Same coupling as Lemma LP289.1, but among possible logs $C$ giving $\varrho_C(t) = \tau$ pick the one minimising $w(C) := \sum_i (s+1-i) q_C(v_i)$. Show $q_C(v_i) = i$, otherwise a swap of two non-lopsidependent consecutive resamplings gives a smaller $w$, contradicting minimality. The $\tau$-check then passes.

nodes.name: Setup: shared random sequences and minimal $w(C)$
nodes.statement: Fix the random sample sequences $P^{(0)},P^{(1)},\ldots$. Among logs $C$ producing $\tau = \varrho_C(t)$, choose one minimising $w(C) = \sum_{i=1}^s (s+1-i) q_C(v_i)$.

nodes.name: Swap lemma for non-lopsidependent consecutive resamplings
nodes.statement: If $C(j)$ and $C(j+1)$ are not lopsidependent, swapping them yields another valid log $C'$ producing the same $\tau$.

nodes.name: Contradiction argument: $q_C(v_i) = i$
nodes.statement: Assume $q_C(v_i) = j+1$ but $q_C(v_{i'}) \ne j$ for any $i' < i$. Then $C(j)$ and $C(j+1) = [v_i]$ cannot be lopsidependent; swapping them yields $C'$ with $w(C') < w(C)$, contradicting minimality.

nodes.name: Conclude $\tau$-check passes
nodes.statement: With $q_C(v_i) = i$, the $\tau$-check sees the same variable values that made $[v_i]$ a valid violated event at step $i$, so it is violated in the check. Hence $\pr[\tau = \varrho_C(t) \text{ for some } t] \le \prod_v \pr[[v]]$.

nodes.name: Initialize variables uniformly
nodes.statement: for all $P \in \mathcal{P}$: $v_P \leftarrow$ a random evaluation of $P$.

nodes.name: Resampling loop
nodes.statement: while some $A \in \mathcal{A}$ is violated under $(v_P)$: pick an arbitrary violated $A$; for every $P \in \mbox{vbl}(A)$ assign $v_P \leftarrow$ a fresh random evaluation of $P$.

nodes.name: Return final assignment
nodes.statement: return $(v_P)_{P \in \mathcal{P}}$.

nodes.name: Initialize variables in parallel
nodes.statement: for all $P \in \mathcal{P}$ in parallel: $v_P \leftarrow$ a random evaluation of $P$.

nodes.name: Parallel resampling loop with MIS selection
nodes.statement: while some event is violated: $S \leftarrow$ maximal independent set in the subgraph of $G_{\mathcal{A}}$ induced by violated events (computed in parallel, e.g. via Luby's algorithm); for every $P \in \bigcup_{A \in S} \mbox{vbl}(A)$ in parallel: $v_P \leftarrow$ fresh random sample.

nodes.name: Return assignment
nodes.statement: return $(v_P)_{P \in \mathcal{P}}$.

nodes.name: Preprocess: bound weights
nodes.statement: Replace $x(A)$ with $\tilde x(A) := (1-\varepsilon/2)x(A)$ and $\varepsilon$ with $\varepsilon/2$ to bound weights away from 1.

nodes.name: Enumerate witness-tree list $L$
nodes.statement: Build $L = \{$witness trees of size in $[c \log m, (k+1) c \log m]\}$; under bounded degree $|L|$ is polynomial in $s$.

nodes.name: Greedy conditional-expectation loop
nodes.statement: for each $(i,j)$ with $1 \le i \le n$, $0 \le j \le c \log m$: for each candidate $d \in D_i$, compute conditional expected number of trees in $L$ that become consistent given fixed samples and $v_i^{(j)} = d$; assign $v_i^{(j)}$ to the value minimising this expectation.

nodes.name: Run sequential/parallel algorithm on fixed samples
nodes.statement: Run Algorithm 1.1 (or 1.2) substituting the deterministic sequences $(v_i^{(j)})$ for the random source; by construction it terminates in polynomial time and returns a non-violating evaluation.

nodes.name: Tightness of the resampling bound
nodes.statement: The bound $x(A)/(1-x(A))$ is tight only in the trivial case where $A$ is isolated in the dependency graph and $x(A) = \pr[A]$; otherwise the labels at any level of a contributing witness tree must form an independent set, ruling out equality.

nodes.name: Implementation primitives required
nodes.statement: Sequential version requires a sampler for $\mathcal{P}$ and an oracle that finds the violated events; parallel version additionally needs a parallel MIS routine. Luby's algorithm gives expected $O(\log^2 m)$ time for the MIS work.

nodes.name: Derandomization without bounded degree
nodes.statement: Is it possible to derandomize the Moser-Tardos algorithm even when the maximum degree of the dependency graph is unbounded?

nodes.name: Constructive LLL feasibility problem
nodes.statement: Given a finite family $\mathcal{A}$ of events on a finite set $\mathcal{P}$ of mutually independent random variables (with $\mbox{vbl}(A)$ accessible for each $A$), efficiently find an evaluation of $\mathcal{P}$ violating no event in $\mathcal{A}$, under LLL-type bounds on $\pr[A]$.

nodes.name: Hypergraph 2-coloring under bounded edge intersections
nodes.statement: Hypergraph in which every edge has $\ge k$ vertices and shares vertices with $\le 2^{k/48}$ other edges admits a polynomial-time 2-coloring without monochromatic edge (Beck 1991); subsequent work raised the threshold to $2^{k/8}$ (Alon), $2^{k/4}$ (Srinivasan), $2^{k/2}$ (Moser 2008a), $2^k/32$ (Moser 2008b).

nodes.name: SAT with bounded variable occurrences via lopsided LLL
nodes.statement: In a CNF formula, two clauses are in \emph{conflict} if one contains literal $l$ and the other $\bar l$. The (elementary) violation events of conflicting clauses are lopsidependent; merely overlapping clauses are not. Berman-Karpinski-Scott [BKS03] used the lopsided LLL to bound the allowed number of occurrences per variable while guaranteeing satisfiability; this proof can be made constructive via the present method.
